newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO wins Fed approval for SFB buy.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO wins Fed approval for SFB buy.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Thursday the Federal Reserve Board in Washington had approved its planned acquisition of Standard Federal Bancorporation Inc, its largest to date.
"To ABN AMRO the approval by the Federal Reserve marks an important step forward in the process of acquiring Standard Federal," ABN AMRO said in a statement.

"The next step is to obtain approval from Standard Federal's shareholders," it said, adding it expected the acquisition process to be finalised in the second quarter of 1997 -- slightly earlier than initially foreseen.
ABN AMRO announced last November its US subsidiary ABN AMRO North America had reached agreement on the takeover of Standard Federal, the largest savings bank in the U.S. Midwest.
Under the deal ABN AMRO is to offer $59 per share for Standard Federal's outstanding share capital, taking the value of the acquisition (including costs) to some $1.9 billion.

Standard Federal, based in Troy near Detroit, Michigan, has 182 branches in Michigan, Illinois, Ohio and Indiana. ABN AMRO said its area of operations fitted well with that of ABN AMRO's LaSalle group in Illinois.

The Standard Federal branches will continue to operate under their own name, except in Illinois where they currently operate as Bell Federal and will later be integrated into LaSalle Bank's FSB branch network, ABN AMRO said.
